versions.vendor_benchmark_code: mem0ai/memory-benchmarks@4b61c5d31b9c668a12b4f5e78064248a02c82d2b, benchmarks/locomo/run.py (ingest_conversation, session_to_chunks, process_question), benchmarks/longmemeval/run.py and benchmarks/beam/run.py (CHUNK_SIZE), benchmarks/common/mem0_client.py
versions.resolved_dependencies: uv.lock resolved 2026-10-05 with exclude-newer and no prereleases: qdrant-client 1.19.1, openai 3.24.0, spacy 3.8.16, fastembed 0.8.1, posthog 7.62.1. pip install mem0ai resolves the same way; mem0's poetry.lock is not used by its hatch build.

entity-h2h.notes: The pinned recipe with the LLM set to gpt-6.2-sol for the entity-resolution head-to-head (newest GPT generation the OpenAI API serves on 2026-11-17). is_reasoning_model stays True as in the recipe, so mem0 sends no temperature or max_tokens; the embedder stays at the SDK default. Qdrant collection memories_entity_h2h.

capabilities.time_notes: Memory.add raises ValueError for any non-null timestamp in OSS 2.2.1 (main.py:818, 'Platform-only temporal parameter'), and Memory.search raises for any non-null reference_date (main.py:1447). The shim puts a system message 'This conversation took place at 1:56 pm on 8 May, 2023.' at the head of every add call. The extraction prompt's '## Observation Date' section, which the prompt calls the only temporal anchor, is always the wall-clock date in OSS (configs/prompts.py _resolve_dates), so relative dates may still resolve against today. The session's ISO date is also stored in memory metadata (session_date) and returned as valid_from.

provenance.mechanism: metadata={'source_id', 'session_date'} on every add; mem0 copies it into each memory it creates and returns it from search. Each memory cites the session whose add created it. The extractor also reads the scope's last 10 raw messages and its 10 nearest existing memories, and a later restatement of the same fact is dropped by hash dedup rather than cited, so the list can be incomplete.

capabilities.delete_notes: get_all(filters={user_id, source_id}) then delete(memory_id) for each. Mem0 deletes memories, not sources. The history store keeps the scope's 10 most recent raw messages (fed to later extraction calls as context) and each memory's change log; neither is searchable.
capabilities.readiness: queued: /ingest validates the session and queues it on the namespace's single worker, returning completeness `unknown` at once, because one session of synchronous Memory.add calls can outlast the harness's 600-second request deadline (gpt-5-mini takes about 16 s per call; a 30-turn LoCoMo session at one turn per call is about 8 minutes). /finish waits until the queue drains (bounded by timeout_s, else ready=false) and reports `known`, or `degraded` when any add raised (mem0 falls back to per-record inserts and raises only when none persisted, main.py:1055-1076), with counts in its receipt. A budget refusal stops the namespace's remaining chunks and /finish returns the budget error. /reset cancels queued sessions; one already running finishes into the retired user_id, which nothing reads.
capabilities.namespace: user_id (filters={'user_id': ...} on search and get_all). /reset moves the namespace to a fresh user_id (<ns>.g<n>) after delete_all, because delete_all leaves the scope's recent raw messages in the history store.
capabilities.parallel_notes: memory-benchmarks drives one Memory instance from 10 concurrent workers across conversations (FastAPI threadpool, sync endpoints); the shim serializes calls within a namespace.

ingest_chunking.notes: set per cell at container start; each chunk is one add call and one extraction LLM call

vendor-default.maps_to: Memory.search(query, top_k=20, filters={'user_id'}, threshold=0.1, rerank=False): the SDK defaults (main.py:1397-1400). Hybrid scoring (semantic + BM25 + entity boost) is always on when spaCy and fastembed are installed.

fixed-evidence.maps_to: same call with top_k=200, the largest cutoff memory-benchmarks evaluates (--top-k 200, cutoffs 10,20,50,200), so the harness can pack 8,000 tokens of short memories

agent_surface.version: not built yet: a harness MCP wrapper over this image's mem0ai 2.2.1 SDK (add, search, get_all, delete), because OpenMemory, mem0's own MCP server, is being sunset

deviations_from_vendor_code: memory-benchmarks talks to its own FastAPI server (docker/mem0/main.py) built from mem0's feat/v3-pipeline branch; the shim calls the pinned mem0ai 2.2.1 SDK in process, with the same Qdrant backend. That server passes user_id to search() as a keyword, which 2.2.1 rejects; the shim uses filters={'user_id'}.

The session date goes into the messages as a system line. memory-benchmarks sends timestamp=<epoch> to its OSS server, whose AddRequest model has no timestamp field, so in the vendor's own OSS runs the date never reaches mem0.

Messages keep the harness's role and render content as 'Speaker: text', as session_to_chunks does; when a role is neither user nor assistant the first speaker becomes user and others assistant, the vendor's mapping. Image captions are not sent because the sanitized sessions carry text only.
metadata={'source_id', 'session_date'} is added to every add call for provenance and delete; the vendor sends no metadata.
user_id is the opaque namespace plus a reset generation, not locomo_<conv>_<run_id>.
Extraction model: the recipe uses the SDK default gpt-5-mini; memory-benchmarks' server defaults to gpt-4o-mini.
Search runs once per question at the policy's top_k; the vendor searches once at top_k=200 and slices cutoffs.
Recipe LLM config sets is_reasoning_model=True, mem0's documented override; without it every gpt-5-mini extraction call fails with HTTP 400 (temperature 0.1 unsupported).
capabilities.proxy_refusals: HTTP 402 from the metering proxy maps to the protocol's budget error, HTTP 403 (route outside the allowlist or leak tripwire) to invalid_request

entity_readout.entities: Memory.entity_store rows (spaCy entity texts; a mention joins a row on an exact normalised-text match or embedding score >= 0.95)
entity_readout.provenance: source_id metadata of each linked memory (Memory.get_all); exact
entity_readout.merge: a mention that matches an existing row is linked to that row; no graph store in mem0ai 2.2.1
